newsitem.title: USA: Eight US states opposing Staples merger in court.
newsitem.headline: Eight US states opposing Staples merger in court.

text.p: Eight states were filing papers in federal court Friday opposing the merger of the office superstore chains Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc, an official with the New York State attorney general's office said.

The attorneys general of New York, California, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Virginia, Washington, Ohio and Illionis planned to make the filing as a "friend of the court" brief with U.S. District Court Judge Thomas Hogan, who was considering whether to grant a temporary injunction against the order.

The brief being filed by the states says that the office superstores' main claim is that "a merger of direct competitors whose business strategy depends on high volume and 'low' prices will introduce competition."
The eight states argue the claim is "wholly at odds with the concept of competition embodied in the antitrust laws."

The eight states argue that the only way to keep prices low for consumers at Office Depot and Staples is through "competitive prices and ... all the other benefits that flow from competition within the unique competitive arena which the office supply superstores represent."
